items.description:
Teams building agentic applications, multi-tenant platforms,
development environments, and CI/CD systems have often had to stitch together
custom infrastructure to run untrusted code safely, preserve state across
sessions, and handle bursty demand without paying for idle capacity. Azure
Container Apps Sandboxes addresses that challenge with a new first-class resource
type in Azure Container Apps that provides fast, secure, ephemeral compute
environments with built-in suspend and resume capabilities. Each sandbox runs in its own hardware-isolated microVM
boundary, supports standard OCI container images, and starts in sub-second
time. It can preserve memory, disk state, and preloaded libraries in a
snapshot, so workloads resume quickly from the same point without incurring a
cold start reload penalty. For technical practitioners, this means they can now
run AI-generated or otherwise untrusted workloads in strongly isolated
environments, preserve execution context across long-running tasks, and scale
from zero to thousands of concurrent sandboxes using the same Azure foundation
that also powers offerings such as GitHub Sandbox, hosted agents in Foundry
Agent Service, and Azure Container Apps Express. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Container Apps Sandboxes

items.description: We are excited to announce the General Availability of Simple log alerts in Azure Monitor, available starting today. This feature is designed to provide a simplified and more intuitive experience for monitoring and alerting, enhancing your ability to detect and respond to problems in near real-time. Unlike Log Search Alerts that aggregate rows over a defined period, Simple Log Alerts evaluate each row individually.Key Benefits:Simplified Query Language.Low Latency Alerting.Support multiple log plans, including Analytics and Basic Logs.Pricing Information:The cost for Simple log alerts is based on 1-minute frequency Log alert.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Simple log alerts in Azure Monitor

items.description: We’re excited to announce the General Availability of Dynamic threshold for Log search alerts! Using dynamic thresholds means you don't have to know the right threshold for each Log alert rule - Dynamic thresholds calculate the most appropriate thresholds for you.Key benefitsDynamic thresholds apply advanced machine learning and use a set of algorithms and methods to:Learn the historical behavior of log query results.Analyze these results over time and identify hourly / daily / weekly seasonal patterns.Calculate the most appropriate thresholds for log alert rules.Adapt automatically to changes in data patterns and adjust the threshold accordingly.At-scale monitoring - in rule monitoring multiple dimensions - the Dynamic threshold is calculated individually, per dimension combination.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Dynamic threshold for Log search alerts

items.description: A new Azure portal experience for Summary Rules in Log Analytics is now available. Summary Rules enable aggregation of high-volume log data at a defined cadence and store it in summarized tables for improved query performance, reporting, or enhanced data privacy. Also, you can ingest logs at lower tier and summarize the important data you need in Analytics tier.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Log Analytics Summary Rules experience

items.description:
Developers
building Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers often rely on plain text
responses even when user interactions required richer experiences, such as
visual data exploration, complex configuration, real-time status monitoring, or
multi-step workflows, which leads to excessive back-and-forth and limited
usability. 
Azure Functions now supports building and hosting MCP Apps using
the Azure Functions MCP Extension. MCP Apps enable servers to return
interactive user interfaces that render directly within chat experiences,
including forms, dashboards, and rich media viewers. This capability is
available for Python, TypeScript, .NET, and Java, allowing developers to build
MCP Apps using familiar languages.
With MCP Apps on Azure Functions, developers can now deliver richer and
interactive experiences directly in conversations, reducing conversational
friction, streamlining complex workflows, and making it easier for users to
explore data and monitor live information without leaving the chat.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Functions now supports hosting MCP Apps

items.description: Rolling updates are now generally available in the Flex Consumption plan, delivering zero-downtime deployments with a simple configuration change.Instead of forcefully restarting all instances during code or configuration updates, the platform gracefully replaces live instances by draining batches every few seconds while dynamically scaling out the latest version to meet demand. This approach ensures uninterrupted execution and resilient throughput across HTTP, non-HTTP, and Durable workloads - even during intensive scale-out scenarios.How to enable:In the Azure Portal, enable it from the Configuration blade Update your ARM/Bicep template with `properties.functionAppConfig.siteUpdateStrategy.type` set to `RollingUpdate`For Durable Functions, configure an orchestration match strategy (see guidance).Known limitations:Scale-out issues may occur with low HTTP concurrency; recommended value is 16.No automatic rollback; roll forward by redeploying the last healthy version.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Rolling updates in Flex Consumption

Azure
Functions now includes managed connectors - the same 1,400+ connector ecosystem
behind Logic Apps and Power Platform - as first-class triggers and
operations. This enables customers to build integrated systems across
the broader ecosystem such as Office 365, Teams, SharePoint, Salesforce, and
other SaaS services, using familiar Functions workflows. With
connectors natively available, developers can build event-driven integrations
without custom polling logic or manual SDK integration, simplifying development
and reducing integration friction. This
feature eliminates the need to build custom integration logic, enabling direct
connections to services like Microsoft 365, Salesforce, ServiceNow, SAP,
Dynamics, and 1400+ other systems. You can now write event-driven Functions
that respond to SaaS events or output to external systems using familiar
Functions syntax, reducing integration complexity and time-to-market. Learn more: Azure Functions
integration with managed connectors documentation  Azure Functions
integration with managed connectors in Azure Functions samples
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Functions now includes managed connectors to integrate with 1400+ of your favorite systems

items.description: Azure Functions now supports building AI agents as a first-class workload using a markdown-first programming model in public preview. With this release, developers can author event-driven serverless agents in natural language. The serverless agents runtime helps developers build agents that respond to conversations, react to events, and take actions across enterprise systems without writing framework boilerplate or per-service integration code. Developers can use any Azure Functions trigger — HTTP, timer, queue, Service Bus, Event Hub, Cosmos DB, blob, Event Grid, and new connector-backed triggers (Teams messages, Outlook mail, calendar events) — to run an agent. Agents can also call connectors as tools, consume remote MCP servers, run sandboxed code and browser automation in Azure Container Apps dynamic sessions, and optionally expose a built-in chat UI, HTTP chat API, and MCP server endpoint with no extra code. In preview, the serverless agents runtime is supported on the Azure Functions Flex Consumption plan. This enables scale-to-zero economics, managed identity, VNet integration, and Application Insights observability for agent workloads on Azure.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Serverless agents runtime for Azure Functions

items.description: Developers are already using AI coding assistants to build Azure Functions apps today, but the quality of the help varies widely. It depends on which underlying model the assistant is using and how recent its training data is, which means developers often get advice based on outdated APIs, deprecated patterns, or generic guidance that misses Azure Functions best practices. Azure Functions now provides a set of AI assistant plugins and agent skills in public preview that close that gap. With a quick one-step install, developers can equip their AI coding assistant — including GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and Codex — with current, Azure Functions expertise that activates automatically as they work in VS Code, the CLI, and azd. The skills cover the end-to-end developer loop: local setup, project and function creation, deployment with tools, diagnostics for deployment and runtime issues, app health and inventory inspection, and best-practices review of existing Function Apps. They follow the Agent Skills open standard, are grounded in official Azure documentation, and integrate with relevant MCP servers so the assistant always works from the latest guidance and Azure best practices — not whatever its base model happened to learn at training time. The result is more accurate, more consistent, and more current AI assistance for Azure Functions, regardless of which assistant or model the developer chooses.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Copilot-assisted coding & agent skills to build, deploy, and run Azure Functions faster in VS Code, CLI, and azd

items.description: Azure Functions now provides built-in Grafana dashboards. Customers now get a zero-setup, single pane of glass for the health, performance, and scale of their function apps directly in the Azure portal: no Grafana instance to provision, no data sources to wire up, and no extra cost.The default dashboard is purpose-built for Azure Functions and brings together the signals that matter for operating a function app, including execution volume, success and failure rates, latency, resource utilization, scale activity, and recent errors correlated with application telemetry. Customers can duplicate and customize the dashboard to fit their team's needs.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Built-in Grafana dashboards for Azure Functions

items.description: The Azure Functions extension for VS Code now provides a redesigned Create New Project experience in public preview, featuring a rich, visual template gallery that replaces the multi-step Quick Pick wizard with a searchable, filterable view of project templates. Developers can browse templates by language and use case, search across template names, descriptions, and tags, and start from featured templates. A "Generate with Copilot" mode lets developers describe what they want to build and get a project scaffold generated for them. The gallery is populated from a continuously updated, Microsoft-curated catalog of 75+ ready-to-deploy samples that have recently been refreshed across all supported languages, covering common scenarios such as HTTP APIs, event-driven processing, scheduled jobs, data integration, Durable Functions orchestrations, MCP servers, and AI and agent workloads. The release also improves the Run Function App experience with smart, runtime-specific pre-start steps that automatically prepare the project — installing dependencies and building the app as needed — before launching the local runtime, so developers can go from create to running in a single click.  Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: New project templates and template gallery for Azure Functions in VS Code

items.description: Azure Functions now supports Go as a first-class language option in public preview. With this release, developers can author event-driven serverless apps in Go using the Azure Functions Go programming model and SDK, while still benefiting from Azure Functions capabilities such as triggers, bindings, and integrated observability. Go support helps teams that standardize on Go deliver cloud-native APIs, automation, and integration workloads without introducing a second language stack. Developers can use familiar Go tooling and patterns while building Functions that respond to HTTP requests, scheduled events, messaging systems, and storage events. In preview, Go language is supported on the Azure Functions Flex Consumption plan. This enables rapid scaling, pay-per-use economics, and streamlined deployment for Go workloads on Azure. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Go language support on Azure Functions

items.description: Azure Functions on Container Apps has traditionally used platform-managed scaling, where triggers are automatically translated into KEDA scale rules. With the new allowScalingRuleOverride property, customers can now choose to override platform-managed scaling and define their own custom KEDA scaling rules.When scaling override is enabled, the platform skips automatic KEDA rule generation and applies customer-defined scaling rules while continuing to run on the same native Functions on Container Apps architecture, available in API version 2026-03-02-preview and later.This enhancement is especially useful for scenarios where there are gaps in platform trigger support, where automatically generated KEDA rules may lead to unintended scaling behavior, or where workloads require custom queue thresholds, HTTP concurrency tuning, or standardized scaling policies across services.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Override Scale Rules in Azure Functions on Azure Container Apps

items.title: Generally Available: Additional support for OpenTelemetry destinations (New Relic, Dynatrace, Elastic)

to investigate failed requests, latency, retries, WebSocket disconnects,
routing behavior, and backend connectivity problems.  This
gives teams a dedicated, scalable traffic logging surface for scenarios where
platform-level signals alone were not enough to quickly understand

friction, and stronger confidence in running and scaling high-traffic,
business-critical applications on Azure Container Apps.  Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Monitor HTTP traffic in Azure Container Apps

items.description: Customers running regulated or sensitive containerized workloads often need stronger protection for data while it is actively being processed, especially in scenarios that require higher isolation and stricter compliance controls. Confidential Compute in Azure Container Apps provides hardware-backed Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) through workload profiles, extending protection to data in use in addition to data at rest and in transit. With this capability now generally available, teams can run higher-trust workloads in Azure Container Apps with stronger isolation for sensitive data and a clearer path to meeting stricter compliance and data sovereignty requirements. This release enables Azure Container Apps workloads to use hardware-enforced isolation mechanisms that protect sensitive data while it is being processed and help prevent unauthorized access to in-memory data, including from the underlying infrastructure. Teams can now deploy confidential workloads on a serverless container platform with stronger protections for data in use. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Confidential Compute support on Azure Container Apps

items.title: Public Preview: Microsoft Defender for Cloud support for Azure Container Apps (Serverless Containers Posture)

items.description: We are announcing the general availability of the Azure Cosmos DB Linux emulator (vNext), a cross-platform, Docker-based emulator for local development and testing against Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL. The vNext emulator runs as a lightweight Docker container on Linux, macOS, and Windows, with native support for both x64 and ARM64 architectures. You can use it to develop and test your applications locally without incurring Azure service costs or needing an internet connection. Since public preview, the emulator has shipped continuous updates that have significantly improved SDK compatibility and expanded Cosmos DB feature coverage. With this release, you get a local development experience that includes support for core operations, a wide range of query capabilities, and added support for vector search and Azure Cosmos DB Shell integration. The emulator also includes health probe endpoints for readiness checks, and OpenTelemetry integration for observability. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB Linux emulator (vNext)

items.description: You can now automate embedding generation from multiple data sources into Azure Cosmos DB and other Azure destinations. Building AI applications often requires stitching together data extraction, embedding generation, and writing to vector databases into a custom pipeline. You have to write extraction logic for each source, integrate with embedding APIs, and build your own sync mechanism to keep embeddings current as source data changes. OmniVec, now in public preview as an open-source project, handles this pipeline end to end, deployed in your own Azure subscription. You configure your data sources, select an embedding model, and deploy with a single azd up command. OmniVec pulls data from sources like Azure Cosmos DB, Azure Blob Storage, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server; generates embeddings; and writes them to Azure Cosmos DB and other destinations on Azure. OmniVec handles content extraction, chunking, and incremental sync out of the box. It supports Microsoft Foundry as well as self-hosted models. You get a web UI, CLI, and REST API for managing sources, models, destinations, and pipelines. The project is MIT-licensed and available on GitHub.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: OmniVec, an open-source embedding toolkit for Azure

items.description: Building AI applications on Azure Cosmos DB just got simpler. With integrated embeddings, now in public preview, Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL can automatically generate and maintain embeddings for your data, without the need to build a separate pipeline. Now you can configure your container's vector embedding policy with one or more source properties, a target property, and a Microsoft Foundry model endpoint. Cosmos DB handles the rest: as items are created or updated, embeddings are generated and kept in sync automatically. Before this announcement, developers had to write integration code to call embedding APIs, build change-tracking logic to keep embeddings current, and manage the glue code that connects data changes to embedding generation. Integrated embeddings removes this entire layer of complexity, letting you focus on your application logic.  Azure OpenAI embedding models via Microsoft Foundry are supported in the initial release. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Integrated embeddings for Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL

items.description:
You can now enable vaulted backups for Azure Cosmos DB
accounts, protecting mission-critical data with secure, isolated, and resilient
backups. Azure Backup for Cosmos DB, now in preview, supports cyber-resiliency
and compliance needs, even in scenarios involving accidental deletion,
malicious activity, or ransomware. With vaulted backups, Azure Backup maintains
an independent copy of your Cosmos DB data in a vault that is isolated from the
source account, strengthening protection against operational and security
risks.  Key capabilities:  Off-site, isolated
protection. Store Cosmos DB backups in an Azure Backup vault, isolated from the
source account to enable recovery even if the source is compromised.  Resilience. Vaulted backups
protect against accidental deletion, insider threats, and ransomware scenarios.
 Policy-based, automated
backups. Configure scheduled backups using Azure Backup policies, reducing
manual efforts and improving consistency. Long-term retention for
compliance. Retain backups for extended durations of up to 10 years to meet
regulatory and audit requirements.  Built-in protections such
as encryption, soft delete, immutability, and role-based access control help
safeguard backup data in the vault.  Billing will be enabled from July
1, 2026.  Learn more: Documentation  Azure Backup pricing Pricing calculator
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Backup for Cosmos DB

items.description: The safe key rotation feature helps you confidently rotate your Azure Cosmos DB account keys by providing visibility into when each key was last used. Without this insight, you risk rotating a key that may still be actively used by your applications, which can lead to unexpected service disruptions. With safe key rotation, you can identify active and inactive keys before taking action, enabling you to make informed decisions and improve your security posture. This capability supports safer migrations, including transitioning to Microsoft Entra ID, by ensuring keys are no longer in use before disabling access. By reducing operational risk and increasing transparency, safe key rotation helps you maintain application reliability while strengthening key management practices.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Safe key rotation for Azure Cosmos DB

items.description: You can now accelerate the development of agentic applications with the new Agent Memory Toolkit for Azure Cosmos DB. This toolkit provides a customizable, code-first solution to help you build scalable, durable, and cost-efficient memory systems for your AI agents, without having to design complex pipelines from scratch. With the Agent Memory Toolkit, you can easily store, update, and retrieve agent memories using a simple interface, while the toolkit handles key tasks such as data processing, embedding generation, and retrieval orchestration behind the scenes using Azure Durable Functions. The toolkit eliminates the need to manually integrate multiple services and simplifies a common architecture pattern used for agent memory systems. You benefit from faster time to production, improved retrieval relevance, and a more consistent and scalable memory foundation for your applications. Whether you are building conversational agents, copilots, or multi-agent workflows, the toolkit helps you focus on your application logic instead of infrastructure. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Agent Memory Toolkit for Azure Cosmos DB

items.description: You can now improve the relevance of any Cosmos DB query or search with the public preview of semantic reranker in Azure Cosmos DB. Semantic reranker analyzes the meaning of your queries and your data to reorder results based on contextual relevance rather than keyword matching alone. This ranking is especially useful for AI-powered applications such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), question answering, and agentic apps. With semantic reranker, you can deliver more precise and reliable results without building complex ranking pipelines or tuning scoring logic manually. It works directly with your existing Cosmos DB queries—including vector, full-text, and hybrid search—enabling you to quickly enhance result quality while maintaining low operational overhead.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Semantic reranker in Azure Cosmos DB

items.description: We are announcing the public preview of the Agentic Retrieval Toolkit for Azure Cosmos DB. Motivated by GraphRAG and multiple-hop reasoning problems, this new capability helps you build advanced retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) applications that go beyond single-pass retrieval by dynamically identifying information gaps and iteratively retrieving additional context. The toolkit combines hybrid search across vector and full-text indexes, diversity-aware document selection, and multiple-round reasoning to produce more complete, grounded responses. With agentic retrieval, you can improve answer quality for complex, multiple-step questions where relevant information is spread across many documents or data sources. The retrieval pipeline adapts in real time by generating follow-up queries, retrieving new evidence, and refining responses until it has sufficient coverage. This approach reduces redundancy, increases recall, and delivers higher-fidelity results for copilots, agents, and knowledge-intensive applications built on Azure Cosmos DB. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Agentic Retrieval Toolkit for Azure Cosmos DB

items.description: Global secondary indexes (GSIs) for Azure Cosmos DB are now generally available, giving you a powerful way to accelerate query performance without adding complexity to your application code. GSIs are read-only containers that automatically stay in sync with your source container using the change feed. Each GSI has its own throughput, partition key, and indexing policy, so you can optimize them for any query pattern. With GSIs, you can convert expensive cross-partition queries into efficient single-partition lookups by storing data under a different partition key. Using GSIs means lower Request Unit (RU) consumption, reduced latency, and better performance isolation for your workloads. You can isolate a subset of your workload, such as creating vector or full-text search indexes in the GSI to support AI applications, without impacting transactional operations on the source container. Adding a GSI to a new or existing container allows you to maintain query efficiency even as your workload requirements evolve.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB global secondary indexes

items.description:
As
organizations build more agentic applications, agent-to-agent communication is
becoming a critical part of enterprise AI systems. But in many environments,
agent traffic operates outside existing API governance layers —
making it difficult to apply consistent security, visibility, and operational
controls.  With
support for JSON-RPC–based A2A APIs, Azure API Management enables platform
teams and developers to manage agent interactions alongside REST, GraphQL,
MCP tools, and AI model APIs using the same API management platform they
already rely on. This allows organizations to apply existing security,
mediation, and governance policies to agent traffic, observe and
trace agent interactions end-to-end, and manage agent APIs within a unified
operational model instead of introducing separate gateways or disconnected
tooling for agents.  By
bringing A2A APIs into the same governance and observability framework as the
broader API ecosystem, Azure API Management helps organizations scale agentic
systems with enterprise-grade security, control, and operational
consistency.  Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure API Management adds support for Agent-to-Agent (A2A) APIs

As organizations adopt multiple LLM providers, developers often need to handle different API formats, SDKs, and integration patterns for each model vendor. This increases application complexity and makes provider switching, failover, and governance more difficult. With the Unified Model API, Azure API Management enables organizations to standardize on a single client-facing API format — such as the OpenAI Chat Completions API — while transparently transforming requests to various backend providers, including OpenAI and Anthropic models. This allows teams to: Use a consistent client SDK and API format across multiple LLM providers Switch or fail over between model providers without client-side changes Simplify application development for multi-model AI architectures Apply centralized governance, security, and observability across heterogeneous model backends By abstracting provider-specific differences behind a unified API layer, Azure API Management helps organizations build more portable, resilient, and governable AI applications. Learn
more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure API Management introduces a Unified Model API for multi-model AI applications.

Modern
integration and automation teams increasingly want the flexibility of writing
workflows directly in code while still benefiting from managed
orchestration, enterprise connectors, and cloud-scale operational capabilities.
Traditional workflow models can create friction for pro developers who prefer
imperative programming patterns and code-first development experiences.  With Codeful Workflows,
Azure Logic Apps extends Logic Apps Standard with a code-first authoring and
execution model built on .NET and a first-class Logic
Apps Standard SDK. This allows developers to:  Implement and structure
workflows directly in code using imperative programming patterns  Develop, and test workflows
locally, running workflows locally and in the cloud.  Leverage Logic Apps
Standard connectors and operational capabilities from code-first workflows Accelerate workflow

items.description: The Azure Cosmos DB all versions and deletes change feed mode is now generally available, giving you complete visibility into every change that happens in your containers. Unlike the default latest version mode, which surfaces only the most recent state of an item, all versions and deletes captures every create, update, and delete operation in the order it occurred, including intermediate changes between reads and TTL expirations. This mode opens up scenarios that were previously difficult to build. You can replicate data between locations without implementing soft deletes, trigger logic on every incremental change even when multiple updates happen between polls, and set up auditing workflows that fire on delete operations. Each change includes metadata identifying the operation type, so your application can handle creates, updates, and deletes with distinct processing logic. To get started, enable continuous backups on your Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL account, which automatically creates the all versions and deletes change log. You can then consume it through the change feed pull model or change feed processor in supported SDKs. Changes are available to read within your configured continuous backup retention period. Learn more.

This feature is an addition to the already existing force promote feature, which immediately promotes a replica cluster in the event of availability loss.Force promote favors availability over consistency and thus does not wait for unreplicated data to make its way to the replica cluster before being promoted. With the graceful promote feature, you can now promote a regional cluster to the primary in the event of changing application traffic patterns. This feature is ideal when there is no availability loss on the primary but simply a change in traffic that requires database requests to be made to the closer regional cluster.Learn more.

Advanced filtering for DiskANN vector search in Azure HorizonDB is now available in public preview. With this release, you can combine vector similarity search with metadata filters such as category, date range, price, or tenant ID without the performance penalties that typically come with filtered vector queries. DiskANN advanced filtering delivers lower latency on filtered vector search compared to traditional approaches, enabling you to build AI-powered retrieval applications that are both precise and fast at scale.  

Whether you are building an agentic application, a product recommendation engine, or an enterprise search experience, you can now apply complex filters alongside vector similarity in a single query and get results in milliseconds, even across millions of vectors. This capability runs natively inside your Azure HorizonDB instance alongside your relational data, eliminating the need for a separate vector database or external search service. You retain full transactional consistency, use familiar PostgreSQL SQL, and benefit from DiskANN's industry-leading performance on disk-resident indexes. Advanced filtering works seamlessly with pgvector, Azure AI integrations, and the broader HorizonDB AI retrieval stack, including BM25 full-text search and graph traversal. Learn more.

items.description: BM25 full-text search is now available in public preview for Azure HorizonDB. Now you can get production-quality keyword search powered by BM25, the same relevance ranking algorithm used by Elasticsearch, Solr, and Azure AI Search, running entirely inside your PostgreSQL database as a native extension. You no longer need to deploy and manage a separate search service to get high-quality text search. The full-text search extension replaces PostgreSQL's built-in ts_rank with BM25 scoring, which delivers significantly better relevance through term frequency saturation, document length normalization, and inverse document frequency weighting. It's faster than native PostgreSQL full-text search with Generalized Inverted Index (GIN) indexes on complex, multi-keyword queries. The extension also supports fuzzy matching for typo tolerance, phrase search with configurable word proximity, and Boolean query syntax (AND, OR, NOT) capabilities that previously required an external search engine. By combining pgvector with DiskANN for vector similarity search, you can now build hybrid search applications that deliver both keyword precision and semantic understanding in a single SQL query using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF). Your data stays in one place, you use familiar PostgreSQL, and you eliminate the operational burden of syncing data to an external search service. Learn more.
