This workflow helps you move from validated schema to a working back end, so you can build faster without switching tools. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Data API builder with built-in GitHub Copilot in MSSQL extension

items.description: The GitHub Copilot integration with Schema Designer is now generally available in the MSSQL extension for Visual Studio Code, expanding the visual schema design experience with AI-assisted capabilities. Based on developer feedback and evolving workflows, this integration enables you to explore, design, and modify database schemas using natural language.You can describe the tables or changes you want, and GitHub Copilot plans and generates proposed updates inside Schema Designer. Each schema change is previewed visually, color-coded, and tracked in a dedicated Change Tracking panel with familiar source control-style labels such as Add (A), Modify (M), and Delete (D). You can clearly differentiate between your own edits and AI-generated suggestions, inspect detailed modifications, and review changes before they are applied.Moreover, Schema Designer now supports ORM script generation for migration, helping you move from visual schema changes to migration-ready scripts more efficiently. Whether you’re starting a new project or updating an existing one, this guided experience helps you move confidently from an idea to a validated data model.From there, you can continue into Data API builder in the MSSQL extension, where GitHub Copilot plans and generates back-end endpoints from your schema. Together, these experiences give you an end-to-end path from database design to a working back end in minutes.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: GitHub Copilot integration in Schema Designer for the MSSQL extension

items.description: In June 2026, the following updates and enhancements were made to Azure SQL: Execute SQL queries, document with Markdown, and mix kernels like Python using SQL Notebooks in the MSSQL extension for Visual Studio Code. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure SQL updates for June

items.description: In early June 2026, the following update and enhancement was made to Azure SQL: Now you can use post-quantum resilient AES 256 symmetric keys to configure transparent data encryption (TDE) with customer-managed keys in Azure SQL Database. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure SQL updates for early-June

items.description: Managing your quota is now faster, simpler, and more transparent. Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server supports self-service quota management through the Azure Quotas blade in the Azure portal. You can view your current quota usage and limits, request quota increases, and track the status of your requests all directly from the portal without needing to file a support ticket. Previously, requesting a quota increase required you to navigate to Help + Support and submit a support request, which could take 24 to 48 hours to process. Now, you can submit quota adjustment requests through the centralized Azure Quotas experience, where eligible requests are evaluated and approved automatically, significantly reducing wait times. This streamlined experience gives you real-time visibility into quota utilization across your subscriptions, helping you plan for capacity needs and avoid deployment interruptions.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server self-service quota management experience

items.description: Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server continues to expand its global footprint with new regional availability and enhanced availability zone support. You can now deploy Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server in the Denmark East, Austria East, and Belgium Central regions, bringing Azure-managed MySQL closer to your workloads with full support for zone-redundant high availability and geo-redundant backup. This update enables you to meet local data residency requirements while taking advantage of enterprise-grade reliability and low-latency access. Additionally, several regions have been expanded with a new availability zone: Taiwan North, Japan West, South Central US, and US Gov Arizona. This support gives you more options for distributing your workloads across physically separate datacenters within the region. You can build resilient, zone-redundant architectures and improve capacity availability for mission-critical MySQL deployments. These updates reinforce our commitment to providing you with a globally distributed, highly available managed MySQL service. To get started, visit the Azure portal to create or migrate your Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server in these regions. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Database for MySQL now available in new regions and expanded availability zones

items.description:
Choosing the right AI system is rarely as simple as picking
the newest or largest model — and agents add their own layer of variability on
top. A model that wins on a public leaderboard can still underperform on the
reasoning, math, or domain-knowledge questions that matter for your
application, and an agent that solves one task well can regress on another
after a prompt or tool change. The only way to know is to measure, on the same
benchmark, under the same conditions, every time something changes. Benchmarks in Microsoft Foundry (preview) make that kind of
measurement a first-class part of the development workflow. You can run
well-known open-source benchmarks against any model deployment or agent in your
project, compare runs side by side in the evaluation group view, and drive the
whole flow from the portal or the REST API.  Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Benchmark evaluations for fine-tuned models in Microsoft Foundry

items.description: Deployment templates in Azure Machine Learning add public preview support for deploying from registries, expanding the set of model registries that customers can use as the source for a templated deployment. Deployment templates package a model, deployment configuration, and container information into a reusable artifact that platform teams can share with development teams. This update makes it easier for platform owners to standardize how a team deploys curated models from registries, while preserving governance through the template itself. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Deployment Templates support packaging deployment configurations in registries for curated deployment

items.description: Deployment templates in Azure Machine Learning add CLI and SDK support in public preview, so platform teams can create, update, delete, and manage templates from infrastructure-as-code pipelines instead of only the portal. The new commands work with az ml deployment-template create, list, show, update, and delete, and the Python SDK exposes the same operations through the azure-ai-ml client. Teams can check deployment templates into Git, review them in pull requests, and manage them through Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions exactly like other Azure resources. They can deploy the model packaged with deployment templates by using az ml online-deployment create or the equivalent operation in the SDK. This enables repeatable, auditable rollouts of standardized model deployments across many projects in an organization without manual portal steps. Learn more
items.title: Public Preview: CLI and SDK support for Deployment Templates

items.description: Speech SDK 1.50 ships as a generally available release across all supported languages: C#, C++, Java, JavaScript, Python, Objective-C, Swift, and Go. The release rolls up the latest speech-to-text and text-to-speech features behind a stable API surface and is published to the standard NuGet, Maven, npm, PyPI, and CocoaPods feeds. Existing apps can move to 1.50 with a package version bump in most cases. The SDK continues to support real-time and offline scenarios against local devices, files, Azure Blob Storage, and input/output streams. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Speech SDK 1.50 for Azure AI Speech

items.description: Microsoft Foundry brings code-first observability to agent developers in public preview, delivered as an observe skill inside the Foundry Plugin for VS Code Copilot Chat. Developers run the full evaluation-driven optimization loop from the editor through natural language commands. The skill orchestrates Foundry MCP tools to auto-generate context-specific evaluators and starter datasets from the agent definition, run batch evaluations, download and cluster failures by root cause, propose prompt improvements, deploy new agent versions, and compare versions side by side. Developers stay in their coding environment instead of jumping to the portal, which shortens the agent development loop and lowers the barrier to consistent observability. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Code-first observability for Foundry Agents in VS Code

items.description:
Microsoft Foundry adds region-agnostic reservations for
Global Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) at general availability, letting
customers commit to PTU capacity once and consume it from any supported region.
Previously, a reserved PTU commitment was tied to a single region, which
created friction for customers that operated multi-region applications or
wanted to shift workloads as traffic patterns changed. With region-agnostic
reservations, finance teams can sign one reservation contract and engineering
teams can deploy models in whichever Azure region best fits a given workload,
with the reservation discount applied automatically. Reservations cover
supported Foundry Models including Azure Direct first-party models such as
GPT-5 and GPT-4.1. Existing region-bound reservations continue to honor their
original terms. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Region-agnostic reservations for Global PTU in Microsoft Foundry

items.description: Microsoft Foundry now offers MAI-Voice-2 in public preview, a first-party voice model from the Microsoft AI team. MAI-Voice-2 generates natural speech across more than 10 languages and supports voice cloning from a short reference sample, plus voice prompting so developers can shape tone, pacing, and style with plain instructions. Customers can build multilingual virtual agents, accessibility experiences, and audio content workflows without stitching together separate cloning and prompt-engineering tools. Because MAI-Voice-2 is sold directly by Microsoft, it ships with the same billing, content safety, and responsible AI policies as other Microsoft-published models in Foundry. Developers can deploy it through the Foundry catalog and call it alongside other speech and language models in a single project. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: MAI-Voice-2 in Microsoft Foundry

items.description: Microsoft Foundry IQ reaches general availability, giving developers a managed knowledge layer that grounds agents in enterprise data without rebuilding retrieval pipelines for each project. Teams connect SharePoint, OneLake, Azure Blob, and other sources once, then Foundry IQ handles ingestion, chunking, vector indexing, and access enforcement using the calling user's permissions. Agents query a single knowledge base and receive ranked, source-cited results, so answers stay tied to the documents customers control. Foundry IQ runs inside the same Foundry project as the agent and shares its identity, observability, and content safety configuration. Customers can ship grounded copilots faster, reduce duplicated retrieval code across teams, and keep sensitive data inside the tenant boundary. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Microsoft Foundry IQ

items.description: Microsoft Foundry IQ adds public preview support for OneLake Catalog as a knowledge source, so agents can ground responses on lakehouse tables, files, and shortcuts already governed in Microsoft Fabric. Data engineers register the OneLake catalog once and Foundry IQ ingests the cataloged items, respecting Fabric permissions and sensitivity labels at query time. Analysts get agent answers that cite the same curated datasets used in dashboards and reports, instead of duplicate copies sitting in a separate vector store. The integration removes a common gap between BI data and AI applications, letting customers reuse their Fabric investment for agent grounding. Setup uses the same connection flow as other Foundry IQ knowledge sources. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: OneLake Catalog integration for Foundry IQ Knowledge Sources

items.description: Foundry IQ knowledge bases now surface document-extracted images at query time in public preview. When ingestion pulls figures, screenshots, and diagrams out of PDFs, slides, and Office files, Foundry IQ retains each image alongside the text it appeared with and can return it as part of a retrieval result. Agents can show the original chart to the user instead of describing it secondhand, so answers about technical diagrams, product photos, and report figures stay anchored to the source artwork. Customers building support assistants, internal research tools, and knowledge portals can render visual context inline without building a separate image pipeline. The capability is available across all Foundry IQ-supported document types. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Image serving in Foundry IQ knowledge bases

items.description: Azure AI Search now supports managed identity authentication for the billing operations it issues against Microsoft Foundry resources, replacing the prior key-based flow. Customers assign a system-assigned or user-assigned identity to the search service, grant it the appropriate role on the Foundry account, and skill executions that call Foundry models for embeddings, chat completions, or extraction bill through that identity. Security teams remove another long-lived secret from their environment, simplify rotation, and gain Entra-based audit trails for cross-service calls. The change is available in all regions where Azure AI Search and Microsoft Foundry are colocated, and applies to indexer skillsets that invoke Foundry models. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Managed identity for Foundry billing calls from Azure AI Search

items.description: Azure AI Search makes the GenAI prompt skill generally available, letting indexers call chat completion models during enrichment without custom code. Authors point the skill at a Foundry-hosted model, write a prompt template that references field values, and receive structured output written back to the index. The same chat completion capability is also available inside knowledge sources, so retrieval-augmented agents can run a quick model call against retrieved chunks before returning results. Customers use the skill for content classification, summarization, entity normalization, and field cleanup in the ingestion pipeline, replacing prior workflows that required separate functions or Logic Apps. Authentication supports managed identity, so calls stay inside the customer tenant. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: GenAI prompt skill and chat completion in Azure AI Search knowledge sources

items.description: Content Understanding in Microsoft Foundry now supports an extractionMode setting that lets you choose how documents are analyzed. Pick a layout-aware mode for structured documents where tables, sections, and reading order matter, or a faster text-only mode when you only need clean Markdown for downstream RAG indexing. The same Analyze API call returns field values with confidence scores and source grounding, so downstream automation can branch on whether human review is required. extractionMode is exposed in both the Foundry portal analyzer schema and the REST API, and is part of the GA `2025-11-01` API version. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Content Understanding extractionMode for documents

items.description: The Azure AI Search SharePoint in Microsoft 365 indexer now indexes ASPX site content and SharePoint Lists in addition to document libraries. The indexer connects through a Microsoft Entra application registration with application or delegated permissions, picks up new and changed items incrementally, and removes deleted items on the next run. Inclusion and exclusion rules let you scope ingestion to specific sites, libraries, lists, or folders, and additional columns can be brought through as searchable fields. The same indexer continues to support basic ACL preservation and Microsoft Purview sensitivity label ingestion in preview.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: SharePoint in Microsoft 365 indexer supports ASPX pages and Lists

items.description: Azure AI Search now emits audit events for Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels carried alongside indexed documents. When the SharePoint in Microsoft 365 indexer is configured to preserve and honor sensitivity labels, query-time filtering decisions and label changes flow into Microsoft Purview activity logs. Security and compliance teams can review who queried labeled content, when label values changed, and how those changes affected search visibility. The capability builds on the existing sensitivity label ingestion preview and requires no schema changes to existing indexes. Configure auditing through your Microsoft Purview tenant settings. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Microsoft Purview sensitivity label auditing in Azure AI Search

items.description: Photo Avatar in Azure AI Speech is now generally available in standard and custom flavors. Standard Photo Avatar produces a talking head video from a single photo at 512x512 resolution, and custom Photo Avatar lets you fine-tune the look from your own image with one minute of consent audio for the matching voice. Both modes run through the same batch synthesis and real-time synthesis APIs already used for video avatars, so existing avatar code paths keep working. Photo Avatar is built on the VASA-1 model family and integrates with Voice Live for low-latency, two-way conversational scenarios where you need a face on the agent. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Photo Avatar standard and custom in Azure AI Speech

items.description:
Adaptive
Custom Translation (AdaptCT) is generally available in the Azure AI Foundry
NextGen playground for Azure Translator. AdaptCT enables enterprises to adapt
translations to domain‑specific terminology using small datasets—eliminating
the need for traditional model retraining. AdaptCT allows developers to update
multilingual content in minutes by indexing high‑value examples and applying
them dynamically at translation time (few-shot) to ground selected LLM. This
approach helps organizations: Launch multilingual
product features faster Maintain terminology
consistency across evolving content Reduce operational
overhead for translation workflows Deliver localized customer
experiences at scale AdaptCT
turns translation into an agile enabler for global growth—supporting real‑time
updates across support content, product documentation, and dynamic digital
experiences. Learn
more.
items.title: Generally Available: Adaptive custom translation in the Azure AI Foundry NextGen playground

items.description:
Azure AI
Translator publishes generally available SDKs that target the latest text
translation REST API across four languages: C#/.NET, Java, JavaScript, and
Python. The SDKs expose Translator API v4 SDK to GA across all four supported
programming languages, giving developers a single client surface to choose
between traditional neural machine translation and LLM-based translation per
request. Teams building multilingual products and support content have had to
manage two parallel translation paths, with different SDKs, request shapes, and
quality profiles, making it hard to mix models within one workflow. With the
new SDK, developers can set the translation model, output tone, target gender,
and adaptive settings on every call from the same Translator client. The
release simplifies integration code, makes feature parity across .NET, Python,
Java, and JavaScript clients consistent, and aligns the SDK surface with
Translator API v4 capabilities including LLM model selection and the latest
adaptive translation features.  Learn
more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure AI Translator SDKs for the latest text translation API

items.description: Azure AI Translator now supports synchronous single-document image translation at general availability. Customers can submit a standalone image file (JPEG, PNG, and similar formats) through one synchronous API call and receive the translated result immediately, with original layout fidelity preserved. The service combines OCR and translation behind a single endpoint, so teams no longer need to build and maintain a custom OCR plus translation pipeline. Pricing is clear on a per-image basis, and the feature inherits the enterprise security posture and regional coverage of Document Translation. Common scenarios include real-time translation for mobile apps, retail signage, restaurant menus, kiosks, and form-based experiences. Early customers include Stanley Black and Decker, USCIS, and UD Trucks. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Document translation for image files (synchronous, single document)

items.description: Microsoft Foundry brings Content Understanding into the portal in public preview, ending the context switch to the standalone Content Understanding Studio for everyday work. Developers get Read and Layout playgrounds inside Foundry for OCR text extraction and structural document analysis covering tables, figures, sections, and hyperlinks, all reachable through Foundry model discovery. Prebuilt document and image analyzers appear as first-class Foundry resources, with sample documents, upload, run, and results views in Markdown, table, or JSON. A direct bridge to Content Understanding Studio remains available for advanced workflows like custom analyzer creation, labeling, and performance tuning. Teams building document intelligence solutions can now manage models, agents, deployments, and document analyzers in one workspace. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Content Understanding NextGen in Microsoft Foundry

items.description: Azure AI Search and Foundry IQ Knowledge Sources add incremental SharePoint permissions sync in public preview, keeping document-level, site, and library access control lists current as SharePoint permissions change. Enterprises store business-critical content in SharePoint and expect AI-powered search, RAG, and agent experiences to enforce the same access rules. Today, carrying SharePoint permissions forward into indexing workflows is partial, so downstream AI experiences can drift from current SharePoint state. With incremental sync, permission updates apply on every indexer run, removing the need for full re-indexing when ACLs change. Supported scopes cover document-level ACLs, site (ASPX) ACLs, and list and library ACLs. SharePoint policy evaluation stays out of scope. Security and compliance teams gain a more reliable foundation for enterprise agents and RAG apps built on SharePoint content. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Incremental SharePoint permissions sync for Azure AI Search and Foundry IQ

items.description: Microsoft Foundry IQ now supports external MCP servers as federated knowledge sources in public preview, expanding retrieval beyond data customers index themselves. Teams can register MCP servers from systems like Salesforce, Atlassian, Confluence, and ServiceNow, then query them alongside indexed sources in a single agentic retrieval call. Foundry IQ handles cross-source selection automatically, choosing which sources to consult per query and merging results with citations. Because the federation uses MCP, partners and customers can plug in any compliant server without building a custom connector. Source-system permissions still gate the data, so an agent only retrieves records the calling user can see. This release helps organizations make agents useful against systems of record without copying data into a separate index. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: MCP Server Knowledge Source in Microsoft Foundry IQ

items.description: Microsoft Foundry IQ now treats a Microsoft Fabric Ontology as a federated knowledge source in public preview, giving agents a way to query the semantic layer customers already curate in Fabric. Foundry IQ translates natural language questions into ontology-grounded queries and SQL against the entities, relationships, and bindings the Fabric team has defined, then returns results with citations back to the underlying Fabric tables. Analytics and platform teams can expose governed business definitions to agents without exporting data or maintaining a parallel schema. The source plugs into the same Foundry IQ retrieval flow as document and database sources, so a single agent call can combine ontology-grounded answers with unstructured knowledge. This release helps customers bring trusted business semantics into agentic applications. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Fabric IQ Ontology Knowledge Source in Microsoft Foundry IQ

items.description: Microsoft Foundry observability adds Trace Replay and new trace visualizations in public preview, giving agent developers a faster way to debug multi-step runs. The replay view rewinds a captured trace step by step, showing the model, tool, and inter-agent calls in the order they happened along with inputs, outputs, latency, and token usage. Updated visualizations group nested spans by agent and tool so engineers can spot the step that introduced an error or a latency spike without scrolling through raw OpenTelemetry data. Traces flow into Azure Monitor Application Insights, so teams keep one observability backend for production AI workloads and the rest of their Azure services. Setup uses the existing Foundry tracing configuration.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Trace Replay and trace visualizations for Foundry agents

items.description: This feature introduces end user feedback logging semantics that enables developers to capture structured feedback signals from real users interacting with AI agents—such as thumbs up/down, ratings, or custom annotations—and automatically associates that feedback with the underlying request traces in Azure Monitor. By standardizing how feedback is logged and correlated with agent runs and telemetry, the feature closes the loop between user experience and system behavior, allowing teams to analyze quality, detect issues, and continuously improve models based on real-world usage. Captured feedback flows through existing observability pipelines, making it available alongside performance and evaluation metrics, and can be fed into downstream evaluation and optimization workflows so that production signals directly inform ongoing model tuning and product iteration. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: User feedback logging in Microsoft Foundry

items.description: Azure AI Speech brings the Custom Avatar and Custom Video authoring experiences into the Microsoft Foundry portal in general availability. Approved customers can upload an actor's video recording, fine-tune a custom video avatar, and generate synthetic talking-head videos through the same Foundry project that runs their text-to-speech and Voice Live workloads. The portal also supports Photo Avatar, where a single reference image plus the Microsoft VASA model produces a head-only avatar. Customers can pair an avatar with a custom neural voice, a personal voice, or the new voice-sync-for-avatar option, then call the result through batch or real-time synthesis APIs. Custom Avatar remains a Limited Access feature gated by responsible AI review and an intake form. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Custom Avatar and Custom Video portal in Microsoft Foundry

items.description: Microsoft Foundry adds Azure SQL Database as a first-class Knowledge Source in Azure AI Search, available in public preview. Enterprise developers and solution architects building Copilot, RAG, and agentic experiences can now expose authoritative tables and views from Azure SQL as searchable, retrieval-ready knowledge for Knowledge Bases, RAG pipelines, and Foundry agents. The capability uses the same indexer-based ingestion patterns developers already know in Azure AI Search and aligns Azure SQL with SharePoint, OneLake, and other Knowledge Sources under one configuration model. Copilots and agents can ground responses in current operational data, including customer profiles, transactions, and reference tables, without custom pipelines or duplicate retrieval systems. The result is a unified knowledge layer where structured business data and unstructured content are queried through a single framework for more accurate, enterprise-ready AI. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure SQL as a knowledge source in Foundry IQ

items.description: Microsoft Foundry brings Azure API Management support to all Foundry model integrations in Azure AI Search, now in public preview. Enterprise platform engineers and AI solution teams running large-scale RAG pipelines can place Foundry and Azure OpenAI models behind APIM for the GenAI Prompt Skill, embedding models, and vectorizer operations used at indexing and query time. APIM provides traffic shaping, load balancing, custom domains, identity governance, and private connectivity in front of every model endpoint a Search workload depends on. Customers can eliminate indexing failures caused by endpoint throttling or outages, stabilize high-throughput ingestion, and consolidate authentication and policy management into a single control plane. Operations teams gain consistent observability and audit trails across enrichment dependencies, while RAG systems hold accuracy and freshness as content volume grows. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: APIM Support for Foundry Models in Azure AI Search

items.description: Microsoft Foundry adds connectors and time-based triggers to the Foundry Tools toolbox in public preview, giving enterprise developers and automation engineers a native way to build event-driven AI agents. Foundry agents today are invoked only through direct API calls or user interactions, leaving teams to build custom orchestration outside Foundry whenever an agent needs to react to a business event. With this release, agents respond automatically to events from Microsoft 365, Azure, and third-party systems, and fire on schedules such as every day at 7am. Developers use the same centrally managed toolbox endpoint for discovery and authentication, while admins retain governance over which connectors and triggers are approved for enterprise use. Reactive, event-driven agent automation now ships without custom orchestration code or per-connector integration work. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Toolbox connectors and triggers in Microsoft Foundry

items.description: Microsoft Foundry brings self-serve custom photo avatar creation to GA in the Foundry NextGen fine-tuning portal. Enterprise customers building voice agents with avatars or producing content with avatar and speech often need a branded avatar instead of a standard one, but until now the only path ran through a manual white-glove engagement that was slow and dependent on internal teams. With this release, customers create custom photo avatars directly in the portal through a guided self-serve workflow, integrated alongside other model customization capabilities in NextGen fine-tuning. Teams iterate on a brand-aligned avatar in hours rather than weeks and deploy to production scenarios such as customer-facing voice agents and interactive training content, removing the bottleneck that limited avatar creation to a small number of partners. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Self-serve custom photo avatar creation in Microsoft Foundry

items.description: Microsoft Foundry adds tool search to Foundry toolboxes in public preview, giving developers and admins a fast way to find the right tool inside large, multi-team catalogs. As your toolbox grows, sending every tool definition on every turn gets expensive. Tool Search retrieves only the most relevant tools at runtime, keeping the model’s context focused and efficient. Instead of browsing lists, the agent describes its intent, discovers the right tools, and executes. Toolbox builders also need control over how tools are surfaced, and tool search provides this. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Tool search in Microsoft Foundry toolboxes

items.description: Azure AI Search and Foundry Knowledge Bases now support private, end-to-end network connectivity between search resources and Foundry services. Customers can route ingestion, enrichment, retrieval, and agent traffic over Shared Private Link or Network Security Perimeter so data never traverses the public internet. This release is built for organizations running RAG pipelines, Knowledge Bases, and Foundry agents on regulated or sensitive data, where compliance teams require full network isolation. Existing search indexes, indexers, and Knowledge Base configurations continue to work; customers add private connectivity through the portal or ARM templates. Combined with Azure RBAC and customer-managed keys, this brings Foundry knowledge workflows in line with the same network controls already used for Azure AI Search production deployments. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Private Connectivity for Azure AI Search and Foundry Knowledge Bases

items.description: Azure AI Speech is rolling out an updated Neural HD text-to-speech model, moving customers from DragonHDLatest to HDv2.5. The update raises audio quality scores, adds style and paralinguistic tag support for English voices, and reduces word error rate in secondary locales such as Spanish, French, German, and Japanese. Customer-facing voice experiences (call center agents, IVR menus, assistant readouts) sound more natural and expressive without changes to the calling code; the existing endpoints and SSML markup continue to work. Speech teams operating multilingual deployments get more consistent quality across markets, which reduces the gap between primary and secondary languages. HDv2.5 is rolling out in public preview across existing Neural HD regions; rollout completes alongside the broader Speech monthly update cycle. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Neural HD voice update (HDv2.5) in Azure AI Speech

items.description: Azure AI Search now offers a serverless option for native indexers in public preview, removing the requirement to provision and manage indexer compute for ingestion workflows. Indexer execution scales with workload demand, so customers stop paying for idle capacity during off-peak hours and stop over-provisioning to handle bursts. The MVP supports document ingestion and enrichment patterns commonly used in RAG pipelines, Foundry Knowledge Bases, and AI-driven applications backed by Azure AI Search. Existing native indexer definitions continue to work; customers opt into serverless execution on a per-indexer basis and keep their current data sources, skillsets, and target indexes. The release is aimed at enterprise developers and platform engineers running large or bursty ingestion jobs who want lower operational overhead and usage-aligned cost.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Serverless indexers in Azure AI Search

items.description: Microsoft Foundry adds MAI-Image-2.5 to the model catalog in public preview, the next generation of Microsoft's in-house image generation model. The release improves photorealism, prompt fidelity, and generation speed compared with MAI-Image-2, and is tuned for marketing creative, product visualization, and content production workloads rather than open-ended consumer art. Enterprise customers get Foundry-native deployment with the same governance, regional availability, and content safety controls already used for other MAI models, plus consumption-based pricing per image. The model is available through Global Standard deployments and composes with other Foundry capabilities, so teams can chain image generation with grounding, retrieval, and agents inside a single workflow. Learn more
items.title: Public Preview: MAI-Image-2.5 in Microsoft Foundry model catalog

items.description: Microsoft Foundry adds MAI-Transcribe-1.5 to the model catalog in public preview, Microsoft's next-generation speech-to-text model. The release adds improved accuracy with noticeably lower word error rate on long-tail locales than the previous generation, plus faster real-time and batch transcription with predictable latency. Target workloads include call center analytics, media captioning, voice agent transcription, and meeting recording. MAI-Transcribe-1.5 is available via Global Standard deployments with Foundry-native governance, regional support, and content safety controls shared across MAI models. It is available through Azure Speech. Learn more
items.title: Public Preview: MAI-Transcribe-1.5 in Microsoft Foundry model catalog

items.description: Azure AI Search adds Microsoft Purview sensitivity label support to knowledge sources in public preview. Labels applied at the source system flow through ingestion into Azure AI Search and into the knowledge bases that ground Foundry agents and copilots, so chunk retrieval, vector search, and multi-step agent reasoning all respect the same access and privacy classifications defined by enterprise security teams. Customers building secure agentic workflows over regulated data get end-to-end label fidelity instead of having to rebuild access enforcement at the retrieval layer. The capability is a prerequisite for downstream Purview-aware agent orchestration scenarios. Existing knowledge sources continue to work; sensitivity awareness turns on per source. The release covers indexed Purview-labeled content surfaced through the Knowledge Source API. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Purview sensitivity labels in Azure AI Search knowledge sources

items.description: Hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service are now generally available, running on Azure Developer Compute with microVM-level isolation. You bring a container-based agent built with the Microsoft Agent Framework or any third-party SDK, and the platform operates it: no manual start and stop, no always-warm instances to pay for, and no hosting infrastructure to patch. Every agent session executes in its own isolated sandbox with a clean environment and strong compute boundaries between tenants, so there is no shared state or cross-session data leakage, which matters for financial, healthcare, and legal workloads. Pre-built snapshots deliver session starts in under 100 milliseconds, Microsoft Entra identity and virtual network support reach internal data and APIs privately, and regional data residency is available across roughly 20 Azure regions. Agents are suspended between conversation turns, so you pay only for active execution. To get started, deploy your container-based agent to Foundry Agent Service. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service

items.description:
Microsoft Foundry Agent Service is now generally available
for Voice Live integration, allowing developers to connect real-time
speech-to-text and text-to-speech to a Foundry Agent without writing their own
audio pipeline. Existing agent capabilities — including tool calling,
knowledge, memory, guardrails, and enterprise integrations — continue to work
seamlessly and are now enhanced with low-latency speech interactions. The agent
provides a real-time streaming voice channel with interrupt handling, turn-taking,
barge-in support, connection management, natural voices, and avatars for
production phone and web experiences. For customers building customer service
agents, learning companions, and in-car assistants, this provides a single
supported path from Foundry agent logic to live audio input and output, instead
of requiring them to stitch together Speech, the agent runtime, and WebRTC on
their own.  Learn
more.
items.title: Generally Available: Voice Live integration with Microsoft Foundry Agent Service

items.description: Azure AI Search adds Microsoft Purview admin access auditing for sensitivity-labeled content in public preview. Admin operations that touch Purview-labeled documents inside Azure AI Search, knowledge retrieval, and Foundry IQ knowledge bases now flow into Microsoft Purview's unified audit log alongside Microsoft 365 events. Security and compliance teams running AI Search in regulated industries get end-to-end visibility for the same admin actions they already track in SharePoint, Exchange, and OneDrive, instead of having a blind spot on the search and agentic retrieval surface. The capability covers index management, source configuration, and access changes on labeled content, and respects existing Purview retention and access controls. Existing AI Search resources gain auditing without code changes. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Purview admin access auditing for sensitivity-labeled content in Azure AI Search

items.description: Microsoft Foundry refreshes the Foundry Memory public preview with a redesigned storage model, new retrieval controls, and tighter integration with the Foundry Agent Service tool surface. Agents using Memory can now write, search, and update user-scoped and session-scoped memories through a single tool, with built-in semantic deduplication and TTL controls that keep memory stores from drifting over time. The refresh adds region availability, content safety filtering on memory writes, and improved observability so memory reads and writes appear as first-class spans in Foundry tracing. Customers running pilots on the previous Memory preview continue to work; the refresh ships as an opt-in upgrade in the Foundry portal and through the agent tool catalog. The release targets agents that need stable user context across multi-turn and multi-session interactions. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Foundry Memory preview refresh

items.description:
Azure AI
Translator's unified Text Translation API reaches general availability, giving
developers a single endpoint that fronts neural machine translation, large
language model translation, small language model translation, Adaptive custom
translation, and classic Custom Translator. Applications send one request and
pick the engine that best fits each piece of content based on language pair,
latency target, and quality requirements. The unified API consolidates years of
customer feedback asking for fewer SDKs and less plumbing between translation
modes. Existing v3 customers can stay on the v3 GA endpoint, while teams that
want LLM-grade quality on long or domain-specific content can opt into the new
GA API and pay only for the requests routed to LLM. The service retains
regional data residency, Microsoft Entra authentication, and per-region service
endpoints.  Learn
more.
items.title: Generally Available: Unified Text Translation API in Azure AI Translator

items.description:
Azure Policy now provides centralized governance for deployments using the model router. Organizations can define and enforce routing standards across their environment, helping ensure that model selection aligns with security, compliance, and operational requirements.
Built-in policy definitions allow teams to govern deployment regions, approved model lists, required routing rules, and logging configurations. Administrators can apply policies across management groups and subscriptions, identify deployments that drift from approved configurations, and remediate issues using existing Azure governance workflows.
Because the integration is built on Azure Policy’s native framework, customers can use familiar tools for compliance monitoring, exemptions, remediation, and reporting without additional engineering effort. This enables regulated organizations to adopt new models more quickly while maintaining consistent governance and control across the enterprise. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Policy Coverage for Model Router in Foundry Models

items.description: Microsoft Foundry introduces rubric evaluators for measuring agent quality, now in public preview for single-turn and multi-turn agent flows. Rubric evaluators enable developers to define context-specific evaluation criteria using agent prompts, production traces and context-specific files with weighted dimensions and optional human review, ensuring that quality is measured against what truly matters for each scenario. This establishes a reliable baseline that is powering downstream workflows, including evaluation, optimization, regression testing and deployment gates.  Learn More
items.title: Public Preview: Rubric evaluator in Microsoft Foundry

items.description: Azure AI Search now supports Content Understanding chunking and image verbalization in public preview, expanding the built-in skill that parses rich documents during indexing. Indexers can split documents into semantically meaningful chunks and generate text descriptions of embedded images, charts, and diagrams in the same pass. Retrieval-augmented generation apps benefit because each chunk carries the visual context that used to be lost when images were stripped out. Customers indexing slide decks, technical manuals, and scanned forms get higher answer quality without running a separate vision pipeline. The skill plugs into existing integrated vectorization workflows, so teams can add it to current skillsets without rebuilding indexes from scratch. This release ships under the same Azure AI Search billing and data residency commitments customers already use today. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Content Understanding chunking and image verbalization in Azure AI Search

items.description: Azure AI Language brings the next-generation Text Analytics for Health (TA4H) playground to general availability in the Microsoft Foundry portal. Clinical informatics teams and ISVs can paste discharge summaries, doctor's notes, or research abstracts and see extracted diagnoses, medications, symptoms, and time references with UMLS entity linking and relation extraction in a single view. The playground returns FHIR-structured output alongside the standard JSON response, so teams can validate downstream integration with electronic health record systems before writing a line of code. Supported input languages, entity categories, and assertion detection match the production service. The same Foundry resource powers both the playground and the REST API. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Text Analytics for Health NextGen Playground in Azure AI Language

items.description: Azure AI Speech moves the Custom Voice authoring experience into the Microsoft Foundry portal in general availability. Approved Custom Voice customers can now upload voice talent recordings and consent statements, run data quality checks, train neural voice models, and deploy to endpoints from the same Foundry project that hosts their text-to-speech, Speech-to-text, and Voice Live workloads.  They can also train Personal voice in Foundry. The experience replaces the previous Speech Studio Custom Voice flow with consistent Foundry navigation, role-based access, and project-scoped resources. Existing custom voice models, test scripts, and endpoints carry over without retraining. Custom Voice remains a Limited Access feature, so customers must already be approved through the intake form before they can use the portal. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Custom Voice portal experience in Microsoft Foundry

items.description: Microsoft Foundry observability introduces intelligent trace filtering and sampling for evaluations in public preview. Instead of running evaluations against all production traces, Foundry now select a representative subset of traces using a multi-stage MinHash farthest-first diversity algorithm, including deduplication, hard filers, aggregation and diversity-based selection for evaluation. This approach improves cost efficiency while producing significantly higher lexical diversity and diverse coverage compared to random sampling. Intelligent sampling is particularly effective for: evaluation and benchmarks, rubric generation and finetuning dataset curation.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Evaluations with Intelligent Trace Sampling

items.description: Microsoft Foundry Agent Service adds agent-to-agent (A2A) communication in public preview for Prompt agents and Hosted agents that use the responses protocol. Agents can call other agents by name through a managed endpoint, with identity, content safety, and audit logging applied to every hop. Developers can model multi-step business processes as a small set of cooperating agents instead of a single monolithic prompt, then trace the full conversation across agents in Application Insights. Because A2A is a first-class protocol in Agent Service, agents written with Agent Framework, LangGraph, or direct code can all participate in the same network without protocol shims. This release helps teams move from single-agent prototypes toward production multi-agent systems with the same enterprise controls already used for individual agents. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Agent-to-agent (A2A) support for Prompt agents and Hosted agents in Foundry

items.description: The Microsoft Foundry extension for Visual Studio Code reaches general availability with a Build 2026 refresh that brings the full model catalog, model playground, and Hosted agent deployment into the editor. Developers can sign in with their Azure account, create or open a Foundry project, browse over 1,900 models with filters for publisher and capability, and deploy a model into the project without leaving VS Code. The extension also generates starter code for Python, .NET, JavaScript, or Java in the SDK and authentication style the developer prefers. For Hosted agents, the extension supports both local development and one-click deploy to Foundry Agent Service, with side-by-side model and agent playgrounds for fast iteration. Learn more
items.title: Generally Available: Microsoft Foundry for Visual Studio Code (June Build 2026 refresh)

items.description: Microsoft Foundry model catalog adds a domain filter in public preview, helping developers narrow the catalog of over 1,900 models to the ones trained for a specific industry or use case. Filters cover domains such as robotics, biomedical sciences, materials discovery, and coding. The filter sits alongside existing filters for publisher, modality, deployment type, and capability, so a developer searching for a robotics-tuned reasoning model can find it in a few clicks instead of scrolling through hundreds of general-purpose entries. The same filter is exposed through the catalog REST API, which lets internal model-discovery portals built on top of Foundry surface domain-specific shortlists for their developer audiences. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Domain filter for specialized model discovery in Foundry model catalog

items.description: Use the Azure Developer CLI (azd) CLI evaluation experience to add a measured quality loop to an agent created with Microsoft Foundry. It empowers users on the hosted-agent lifecycle in azd, where you create, provision, deploy, initialize evaluation assets, run a first evaluation, inspect the run, and reuse the evaluation recipe for later runs. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Observability developer experience in Azure Developer CLI (azd)

items.description:
Enhanced maintenance control capabilities are now generally available for Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server. These new capabilities give you greater visibility and flexibility in managing platform maintenance events, helping reduce disruption to your workloads. 

You can now view upcoming maintenance events directly in the Azure portal, CLI, and APIs, including details such as maintenance type, expected downtime, and deferral eligibility. With the ability to reschedule maintenance by up to 14 days, you can align updates with your business schedules and avoid peak usage periods. Additionally, you can choose to apply maintenance on demand at a time that works best for your environment, improving predictability and control. 

These enhancements eliminate the need for support requests to defer maintenance and help reduce the risk of unexpected downtime, making it easier to operate production workloads with confidence. 

These capabilities are available in all regions where Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server is offered. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Maintenance control for Azure Database for PostgreSQL - reschedule, apply on demand, view and download

items.description: You can now install the DuckDB extension in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Database for PostgreSQL - Flexible Server: DuckDB extension

items.description: Now customers can install the pg_ivm extension in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server pg_ivm extension

items.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL - Flexible Server now supports cross-tenant customer-managed keys (CMK), in public preview, allowing you to encrypt your data at rest using an Azure Key Vault key that resides in a separate Microsoft Entra tenant from the database service. This capability is designed for software as a service (SaaS) providers and enterprises that need to maintain strict separation of duties and ownership of encryption keys, enabling their customers to retain full control over key lifecycle management while PostgreSQL runs in a service provider's tenant. With cross-tenant CMK: 

Your PostgreSQL data is encrypted using a key you own and manage. The database service never has access to your key material. You can rotate or revoke keys at any time without downtime. Authentication between PostgreSQL Flexible Server and the customer-owned key vault is handled using federated identity with Microsoft Entra ID access across tenants. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Database PostgreSQL - Flexible Server cross-tenant customer-managed keys

items.description: You can now use Microsoft Defender security assessments for Azure Database for PostgreSQL to continuously evaluate your database security posture and identify potential vulnerabilities and misconfigurations. This feature helps you strengthen your security baseline, prioritize remediation based on risk, and align with best practices and compliance requirements. You can proactively protect your PostgreSQL workloads with integrated insights directly in Microsoft Defender for Cloud.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Microsoft Defender security assessments for Azure Database for PostgreSQL

items.description: You can now proactively validate Major Version Upgrade (MVU) readiness for Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server before initiating the actual upgrade process. New pre-upgrade validation checks allow you to independently run upgrade compatibility validations and identify potential blockers ahead of time, helping reduce failed upgrade attempts and improve operational predictability. The validation process checks your server against Azure PostgreSQL upgrade policies and PostgreSQL pg_upgrade -check compatibility requirements. It surfaces actionable guidance for issues such as unsupported extensions, replication slots, prepared transactions, configuration mismatches, and other upgrade constraints. You can resolve identified issues, rerun validations as needed, and proceed with the upgrade only when your environment is ready. By shifting validation from inline execution during upgrade to a proactive pre-flight step, this capability helps improve first-time upgrade success rates, reduce troubleshooting effort, and simplify upgrade planning for production workloads.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Pre-upgrade validation checks for Azure Database for PostgreSQL

items.description: You can now convert Oracle database schema objects to Azure Database for PostgreSQL-compatible schema directly in the PostgreSQL extension for Visual Studio Code. The experience provides a project-based workflow for Oracle to Microsoft for PostgreSQL offerings, using Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server as a scratch database for validation and testing during schema conversion. The workflow automatically flags items that can't be converted as Review Tasks, so you can address them before applying the generated artifacts. With this release, you can move schema conversion into a guided Visual Studio Code experience instead of managing the process across separate tools. You can load Oracle schemas, run conversion, validate converted objects, review flagged items, and then apply the generated PostgreSQL artifacts with more visibility into what was converted and what still needs attention. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Oracle schema conversion to Azure PostgreSQL in Visual Studio Code

items.description: In public preview, Microsoft Foundry now supports avatar voice sync with custom voices in the Voice Live API, allowing developers to pair branded or persona-specific text-to-speech voices with real-time avatar experiences. This update helps teams building virtual agents, digital humans, and immersive customer engagement scenarios preserve their existing voice identity while taking advantage of low-latency, lip-synced avatar rendering, removing the previous limitation that restricted avatar pairing to a curated voice set. By unifying custom voices and avatars in a single low-latency pipeline, the capability reduces integration complexity for live conversational scenarios such as kiosks, retail assistants, and accessibility experiences. As a preview, regional availability and configuration semantics may continue to evolve before general availability. To get started, configure your custom voice and avatar in the Microsoft Foundry Voice Live API and review the updated avatar guidance in the documentation. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Voice sync for avatar support in Voice Live API in Microsoft Foundry

items.description: In public preview, Microsoft Foundry now offers an updated TextPII NextGen Playground with a refreshed API Configuration Panel, including preview features introduced at Ignite 2025. This update lets developers test predefined PII categories, redaction modes, and language settings interactively before integrating the API into production workflows. By providing a single interactive environment to validate configurations against sensitive text inputs, the playground reduces the learning curve for new preview capabilities and helps teams govern the AI lifecycle by catching misconfigurations early. The experience supports common PII detection scenarios such as document sanitization, transcript redaction, and dataset preparation for analytics. Preview availability and exact configuration options may evolve before general availability. To get started, open the TextPII playground in Microsoft Foundry and explore the updated configuration panel. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: TextPII NextGen Playground updates in Microsoft Foundry

items.description: In public preview, Microsoft Foundry now offers a Conversational PII (ConvPII) NextGen Playground with transcript input and an API Configuration Panel, enabling developers to validate PII detection across multi-speaker dialogue before integrating the API. This update helps you test conversation-format inputs such as call center transcripts and meeting recordings, iterate on configuration settings, and assess accuracy for informal, multi-turn language. By providing an interactive environment for experimentation, the playground reduces iteration cycles and lowers the risk of shipping misconfigured PII detection into production conversational workloads. The capability targets developers building privacy-aware analytics, support automation, and compliance pipelines that rely on accurate redaction in spoken or chat-based content. Preview availability and configuration options may evolve before general availability. To get started, open the ConvPII playground in Microsoft Foundry and try a sample transcript. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Conversational PII NextGen Playground in Microsoft Foundry

items.description: Azure AI Speech makes the LLM Speech API generally available, delivering state-of-the-art LLM-powered transcription and translation for audio files, with multi-lingual support across 25 languages (90+ locales), improved accuracy, expanded regions, and enhanced prompt-tuning capabilities. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: LLM Speech API in Azure AI Speech

items.description: Microsoft Foundry makes managed virtual network support generally available for evaluations, so customers can run cloud evaluation jobs against models and agents that sit behind private endpoints. The Foundry-managed VNET handles outbound connectivity to the model deployment, the evaluation dataset storage account, and any tool endpoints under test, with no need to maintain bastion hosts or self-hosted runners. Security teams keep network isolation, private DNS, and outbound traffic rules consistent with the rest of their Azure footprint, and audit traces flow through the same Defender and Purview pipelines as production agent traffic. Engineering teams can wire evaluation jobs into CI/CD without opening public network access on protected model endpoints. The capability is on by default for new evaluation runs in supported regions.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Managed virtual network for evaluations in Microsoft Foundry

items.description: Azure AI Search makes OneLake catalog integration generally available for knowledge sources, so customers can register a OneLake item once and reuse it across multiple knowledge sources and agents. The integration honors existing OneLake item-level permissions, sensitivity labels, and lineage, so when a Fabric admin restricts access in OneLake the change flows through to every dependent agent on the next query. Developers pick a catalog entry instead of pasting a path, and the knowledge source picks up schema metadata, freshness signals, and item ownership without extra configuration. Teams already organizing data in OneLake can extend that catalog to Foundry agents and search workloads with no duplicate registration. The integration is available in all regions where Azure AI Search and OneLake operate together. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: OneLake catalog integration for Azure AI Search knowledge sources

items.description:
Azure AI
Translator batch document translation now translates text inside images
embedded in Word `.docx` files as a generally available capability. The service
detects image regions, runs OCR, translates the recognized text, and re-renders
it back into the document while preserving the original layout, font, and
surrounding formatting. Image-aware translation works through the existing
batch translation REST API and SDK paths, with the same source and target Azure
Blob Storage container pattern. Pricing is calculated per image translated,
alongside standard character-based pricing for the surrounding document text.
Output documents are written to the target container in their translated form
for downstream review.  Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Image translation inside Office documents for batch document translation

items.description:
Azure AI
Translator batch document translation accepts image files as a generally
available input type. Supported formats include `.jpeg`, `.png`, `.bmp`, and
`.webp`. The service runs OCR on each image, translates the recognized text
into the target language, and writes a translated image back to your Azure Blob
Storage target container while keeping the original visual design and layout.
Image inputs ride the same async batch REST API, SDK, and managed identity
authentication path as Word, PowerPoint, PDF, and other supported formats.
Pricing is calculated on a per-image basis. Status and per-document tracking
continue through the existing batch translation status APIs.  Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Image file translation for batch document translation in Azure AI Translator

items.description: Azure AI Translator batch document translation ships generally available improvements for PDF translation. The service uses Azure AI Document Intelligence to recover structure from both digital-native and scanned PDFs, then translates the recognized text and re-renders the document with the original reading order, tables, headings, and image placement preserved. The improved pipeline reduces formatting drift in long, multi-column reports and forms, and continues to flow through the standard batch translation REST API with source and target Azure Blob Storage containers. Authentication options stay the same, including shared access signature tokens and managed identity. Pricing follows the existing character-based document translation rates. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Improved PDF batch document translation in Azure AI Translator

These virtual machines deliver significant enhancements over the previous generation Cobalt 100 VMs, offering improved CPU performance, greater scalability, and expanded configuration options to meet the demands of a wide range of workloads. items.description: Microsoft is announcing the preview of multiparty analytics with Azure Confidential Clean Rooms, resulting in fully managed service that allows customers and their partners to securely analyze privacy sensitive datasets with Apache Spark based big-data analytics (Spark SQL) in a confidential computing based environment which protects their raw data from other collaborators and from the Azure operator by performing the computation in a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE). Privacy sensitive datasets include personally identifiable information (PII), protected health information (PHI) and cryptographic secrets.Organizations across industries are increasingly looking to supplement their data with data from business partners, to build a complete view of their business. For example, brands, publishers, and their partners need to collaborate using datasets containing Intellectual Property (IP) to improve the relevance of their campaigns. Data clean rooms help solve this challenge by allowing multiple organizations to share granular data and analyze combined datasets in a secure environment which provides guarantees against exfiltration of raw data.Learn more.
items.title: Private Preview: multiparty analytics with Azure Confidential Clean Rooms

delivered with incoming messages, enabling applications to route events

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Event Grid - MQTT v5 Subscription Identifier

items.description:
Azure Container Linux is a container-optimized, immutable operating system for
AKS node pools — derived from Flatcar Container Linux and built on Azure Linux
RPM packages. It delivers a locked-down, minimal host purpose-built for running
containerized workloads at scale. Key features include: Immutable by design — The root /usr directory is
read-only with dm-verity integrity verification. There is no package manager on
the host — what ships in the image is what runs in production. This eliminates
configuration drift and ensures consistent node state across your fleet. Container-optimized — Minimal OS footprint with
only the components needed to run Kubernetes workloads. Out-of-the-box security — SELinux in enforcing mode applies strict least-privilege policies to all processes. Trusted Launch with a Unified Kernel Image (UKI) verifies boot integrity from firmware through kernel, ensuring nodes haven't been tampered with before they join your cluster. Derived from Flatcar — Built on Flatcar Container Linux's proven architecture: declarative node configuration, systemd-first service management, and an operational model designed for fleets of immutable nodes. Built on Azure Linux — Powered by the Azure Linux RPM ecosystem with Microsoft's security patching cadence, CVE response SLAs, and integrated support through Azure. Learn more and get started:  Tech Community blog post Azure Container Linux Documentation Azure Linux Documentation Azure Linux on GitHub
items.title: Azure Container Linux (ACL) now generally available on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)

items.description:
Azure Linux 4.0,

available in public preview for Azure Virtual Machines and VM Scale Sets. It brings a modernized stack — including Linux kernel 6.18 LTS, dnf5 package
manager, glibc 2.42, OpenSSL 3.5, and Python 3.14 — optimized for Azure
compute, storage, and networking. It delivers faster VM startup and
provisioning with a reduced package footprint and a security-first design.   Key highlights: Azure-tuned kernel — Linux 6.18 LTS with improved Hyper-V integration, GPU/AI accelerator
support, and new hardware drivers Secure by default — Secure Boot, Trusted Launch, SELinux support, kernel hardening, and
SBOMs published with target SLSA Level 3 Minimal footprint — Ships only the packages required for cloud workloads, reducing attack
surface from day one No additional OS licensing cost — Included with Azure compute; no separate OS licensing fees or support
contracts Microsoft-owned supply chain — From kernel to CVE response, enabling fast-track Critical/High CVE
patches with monthly security updates Predictable lifecycle —full support with LTS kernel and annual HWE kernel updates for new
hardware platforms Container images — Base, and distroless images available on Microsoft Container Registry
(MCR) Learn more:Azure Linux 4.0 Build blog post   Azure Linux on GitHub Release notes

announce that Azure Migrate now generally supports discovery and assessment

 Discover and review

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Files assessments are now available worldwide using Azure Migrate

items.description:
Azure Backup now supports snapshot-based backup for SQL Server running on Azure Virtual Machines. This new capability uses Azure disk snapshots combined with native SQL transaction log backups to deliver near-instant, low-impact full backups for large SQL databases, significantly improving backup performance and reducing the load on production workloads compared to streaming backups. You can protect multiple databases under a SQL instance with a single policy and restore using different mechanisms with point-in-time recovery enabled by log chaining on top of snapshot recovery points.All restore points get stored in Azure Recovery Services Vault which provides long term retention and added security for your data in case of Ransomware attacks and any other disasters.Learn
more.
items.title: Public Preview: Snapshot backup for SQL Server in Azure VMs

SQL MCP Server is now generally available, giving customers
a secure, high-performance way to build agentic solutions with controlled
access to production data. Built for SQL and compatible with PostgreSQL and
Azure Cosmos DB, SQL MCP Server is a dynamic, self-hosted data-plane endpoint
with caching, multiple data sources, REST, and GraphQL in one solution. Open

items.title: Generally Available: SQL MCP Server

items.description:
AI pipelines for Azure HorizonDB is now
available in public preview. AI pipelines let you describe an AI data ingestion
workflow, chunking, embedding, extraction, generation, and ranking,
declaratively in SQL, and run it as a fault-tolerant pipeline inside the
database.  Execution is durable: pipelines survive crashes, retry failed steps
automatically, checkpoint incremental work, and resume long-running jobs from
the last completed step. This removes the boilerplate ingestion service that many GenAI
applications rebuild today. Pipelines run on change, so embeddings stay in sync
as source rows are inserted or updated, and only new or changed rows need to be
re-embedded. When the embedding model,
dimensions, or chunk size change, backfill reprocesses every row as a single
durable instance that resumes from the last checkpoint instead of restarting
from zero. AI pipelines are part of the azure_ai extension, built on pg_durable, and work with AI model management, pgvector,
DiskANN vector search, and full-text search to provide an end-to-end retrieval
path inside one database. Learn
more.
